ePramova uses its Facebook page as a main tool for outreach, to promote its original and partner content. Our ability to
reach the audiences declined dramatically after we received a notification from Facebook that our page is at risk of
being unpublished (associated with a post we made). Conversations with Facebook support did not yield any
productive results and did not introduce any clarity.
Detailed description of the situation:
Our typical monthly reach was around 2.5 million users (over the period since the beginning of this year).In the
beginning of May, our coverage was approximately 70k users per day, during May 7-12 we peaked at 524k organic
outreach(through advertising -11,428). The successful outreach during this period is associated with the 9th of May
"Victory day" celebrations and holidays in Belarus and the intense news cycle during the period. Also, one of the videos
posted on 7th of May went viral, contributing to the overall outreach during the period.
On May 14, we received a notification from Facebook that 1 (one) of the posts does not adhere to the community
standards. The post in question included a video of a Belarusian teacher shouting at a student while trying to confiscate
his phone. Link - [link omitted] Needless to say, the purpose of the post was not
to promote violence, but to expose the problems in the Belarusian school system.
Also, on the same day we received a notification that "Page is at risk of being unpublished ". We filed an appeal which
was not approved (May 24). Previously, on May 7th we received a warning related to Facebook Business Account
(advertising account) about imposed restrictions. It is indicated that it is based on a number of violations, however, the
exact violations are not specified. This account has not been used for a long time, since the promotion was performed
by a Belarusian in-country advertising specialist with his own advertising account. We do not know if these events are
related in the general context.
From May 14 (after receiving notifications about the post and about the risk of hiding our pages), our daily reach has
plummeted - to 40k per day, and continued to decline, reaching the low of 16k per day. During the past few days, it
appears that our new "baseline" is about 20k per day.
We are confident that this is not related to our activities (content) or behavior of the audience, since our partners
working in this Facebook niche do not report any similar problems or decline in outreach or other metrics; On the
contrary,they experience further growth associated with the intensified news cycle.
This situation with a sharp drop in our ability to reach the audiences is an extremely serious problem both for us and for
partners with whom we work (who rely on our capacity to reach the audiences), especially in the context of the on-going
repressions and silencing of the media in Belarus on one hand, and a great demand for the content we produce on the
other, as the current news cycle is very intense and significant.
After sending a series of letter to Facebook, we received a call that our situation is being investigated and they will
provide us with an answer in writing; This was the answer we received on May 24, which only stated that our appeal
about the post was rejected; No further communication is expected, and the main issue - sudden decline in outreach is
not addressed

Hi Mike,
I hope you're doing well! Your colleagues here miss working with you.
USAID is forming a more coherent approach to its work in the information space, particularly around the issue of
disinformation and hate speech online, including forming a task team that includes representatives from DRG, from
our new Conflict Bureau as well as Regional Bureaus (and potentially later on from Global Health).
We were hoping that you might be available to talk with us to help us think through the most productive ways
USAID should engage with Facebook on these issues. Would you have some time to speak with us around April
15 or 16th?
Thanks!
Best,
Josh
